canonical_title: Nvidia and major asset managers assemble a $500 billion AI infrastructure financing venture
aliases: Nvidia Wall Street AI infrastructure fund
treatment: Treat the $500 billion compute-financing platform and the August 14 financing-structure details as covered. Reinclude only for binding capital commitments, named financed projects, deployment schedules, changes in participants, closed transactions, or regulatory/financing documents with material new terms.
known_facts: Reuters reported on August 10 at 16:34 UTC that financial firms including Apollo and Blackstone were working with NVIDIA on a roughly $500 billion financing package for AI infrastructure.
The consortium includes BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR.
The capital is intended to support chips, power generation and data-center infrastructure underpinning AI build-out.

By August 14, Reuters reported that NVIDIA had signed memorandums of understanding with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR for compute-financing platforms aimed at raising more than $500 billion in third-party capital.
Jensen Huang said NVIDIA has the option to backstop up to $125 billion, or 25% of potential deals.
Reuters reported Goldman Sachs is the sole lender in the initiative alongside the asset managers and is discussing participation with banks, insurers, money managers and private-credit investors.
The intended structure is an asset-backed market for AI compute rather than the heavier vendor-guarantee model used in some earlier AI infrastructure financings.
reinclude_only_if: NVIDIA or consortium members announce binding capital commitments or closed financings.
Specific data-center, power, chip-purchase or financing projects are disclosed.
The size, capital structure, participant list or deployment timeline materially changes.
Regulatory filings or financing documents reveal material terms.
notes: FOLLOW_UP on 2026-08-14 Night: prior coverage described the platform as still being assembled; new Reuters reporting confirms signed MoUs, NVIDIA's up-to-$125B backstop option, Goldman's lender role, and target investor base.
